content:
I believe I have formalized the following "pushforward of gradings along maps between indexing stets":

Given a module M over a ring R with a grading grM : ι₁ → Submodule R M, and given a map f : ι₁ → ι₂, we obtain an induced_grading : ι₂ → Submodule R M on the same module simply by "regrouping" the summands.

But while the code compiles, there are still parts that look very ugly. And it took me a lot of trial and error to get there. So I'm pretty sure I'm approaching some of this from the wrong angle. I post the code below, and I would be grateful for some feedback.

More specific questions:

  • The key equivalence that "regroups" the summands is called sigmaFiberLinearEquiv below. In defining this, I need to move "indices" back and forth through Mathlib's sigmaFibreEquiv, and I just don't know how to do this correctly. In particular, I still don't know how to prove the lemma sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of without first proving some variant sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of'.
  • In "regrouping summands", I need to talk about the span of a set of submodules of a given module. But there are lots of mathematically equivalent ways of defining this span. How do I find out what the "right" definition is?Which definition should I use if I also want a version of this for, say, additive groups and additive monoids rather than modules over a ring? Currently, I'm using the indexed supremum "⨆" (see induced_decomposition).
import Mathlib
open DirectSum

section DirectSum.of
/- additional _of lemmas for isos already present in Mathlib -/
universe u v v₁ w
variable (R : Type u) [Semiring R]
         {ι : Type v} [DecidableEq ι]

@[simp] lemma DirectSum.sigmaLcurry_of
    {α : ι → Type v₁} [∀ i : ι, DecidableEq (α i)]
    {M : (i : ι) → α i → Type w} [∀ i : ι, ∀ j : α i, AddCommMonoid (M i j)]
    [∀ i : ι, ∀ j : α i, Module R (M i j)]
    (ij : (i : ι) × α i) (m : M ij.fst ij.snd) :
    (sigmaLcurryEquiv R) ((of (fun ij' ↦ M ij'.fst ij'.snd) ij ) m)
    = (of (fun i' ↦ ⨁ (j' : α i'), M i' j') ij.fst) ((of (fun j' ↦ M ij.fst j') ij.snd ) m)
  := by
  exact DFinsupp.sigmaCurry_single ij m

@[simp] lemma DirectSum.lequivCongrLeft_of
    {M : ι → Type w} [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (M i)]
    {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (h : ι ≃ κ) (k : κ) (m : M (h.symm k)) :
    (lequivCongrLeft R h) ((of M (h.symm k)) m) = (of (fun k ↦ M (h.symm k)) k) m
  := by
  exact DFinsupp.comapDomain'_single (⇑h.symm) h.right_inv k m
end DirectSum.of


section DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv
/-
1. Definition of `sigmaFiberLinearEquiv`
   as composition of two isos:
     iso₁ :=  lequivCongrLeft
     iso₂ := sigmaLcurryEquiv
   Each of (iso₁) and (iso₂) are defined in Mathlib,
   and we prove an …_of lemma for each of these.
2. `sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of` lemma, proved from the …_of lemmas for iso₁ and iso₂.
   This is all still very messy and probably not done the correct way.
-/
universe u v w
variable (R : Type u) [Semiring R]
         {ι₁ ι₂ : Type v} [DecidableEq ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₂]
         (f : ι₁ → ι₂)

def DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv
    (M : ι₁ → Type w) [∀ i : ι₁, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι₁, Module R (M i)] :
    (DirectSum ι₁ fun i ↦ M i) ≃ₗ[R] DirectSum ι₂ fun j
    ↦ (DirectSum { i : ι₁ // f i = j} fun i ↦ M i)
  := by
  let hsigma := (Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv f).symm
  let iso₁ := DirectSum.lequivCongrLeft R hsigma (M := M)
  let iso₂ := DirectSum.sigmaLcurryEquiv R
    (δ := fun (j : ι₂) ↦ (fun (i : { i : ι₁ // f i = j}) ↦ M i))
  exact iso₁.trans iso₂

lemma DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of'
    (M : ι₁ → Type w) [∀ i : ι₁, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι₁, Module R (M i)]
    (k : (i₂ : ι₂) × {i₁ : ι₁ // f i₁ = i₂}) (m : M ↑k.snd) :
    (sigmaFiberLinearEquiv R f M) ((of (fun i ↦ M i) (k.snd)) m)
    = (of _ (k.fst)) ((of (fun (i': { i : ι₁ // f i = k.fst})  ↦ M ↑i') k.snd) m)
  := by
  let h := Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv f
  calc (sigmaFiberLinearEquiv R f M) ((of (fun i ↦ M i) (k.snd)) m)
     _ = (sigmaLcurryEquiv R) ((lequivCongrLeft R h.symm) ((of M (h.symm.symm k)) m))
         := by
         simp_rw [h,sigmaFiberLinearEquiv, Equiv.symm_symm, Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv_apply,
           LinearEquiv.trans_apply]
         try rfl -- `rfl` needed in v4.29r8, but no goal here in v4.28.0
     _ = (sigmaLcurryEquiv R) ((of (fun (k : ((y : ι₂) × { x // f x = y })) ↦ M (k.snd)) k) m) := by
         simp_rw [lequivCongrLeft_of,Equiv.symm_symm]
         rfl
     _ = (of _ (k.fst)) ((of (fun (i': { i : ι₁ // f i = k.fst})  ↦ M ↑i') k.snd) m) := by
         rw [sigmaLcurry_of R]

@[simp] lemma DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of
  (M : ι₁ → Type w) [∀ i : ι₁, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι₁, Module R (M i)]
  (i : ι₁) (m : M i) :
    (sigmaFiberLinearEquiv R f M) ((of _ i) m)
    = (of _ (f i)) ((of _ ⟨i, rfl⟩) m) := by
  rw [sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of' R f M (k := ⟨f i, ⟨i, rfl⟩⟩)]
end DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv


section coeLinearMap
/- `coeLinearMap` is the map from the direct sum of some submoduls of M to M.
    We show here that it's restriction to its codomain (the span of those submodules)
    is surjective. -/
variable (R : Type u) [Semiring R]
variable {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
variable {ι : Type v}
variable (grM : ι → Submodule R M)
variable [DecidableEq ι]

abbrev DirectSum.coeLinearMap.codRestrict :
  (⨁ (i : ι), grM i) →ₗ[R] (⨆ (i : ι), grM i : Submodule R M)
  := (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ range_coeLinearMap).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (coeLinearMap grM).rangeRestrict
  -- This is just an `abbrev` so that `simp` and other tactics will unfold it automatically.

lemma DirectSum.coeLinearMap.codRestrict_surjective :
  Function.Surjective (⇑(coeLinearMap.codRestrict R grM)) := by
  simp only [codRestrict, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, EquivLike.comp_surjective]
  exact LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict _
end coeLinearMap


/- MAIN PART:  Construction of induced decomposition -/

variable (R : Type u) [Semiring R]
variable {ι₁ ι₂ : Type v} [DecidableEq ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₂]
variable {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (grM : ι₁ → Submodule R M)
variable [DirectSum.Decomposition grM]
variable (f : ι₁ → ι₂)


def induced_decomposition : ι₂ → Submodule R M
  := fun j ↦ (⨆ (i : { i : ι₁ // f i = j}), grM i : Submodule R M)

abbrev Dec' := ⨁ j, (induced_decomposition R grM f) j
abbrev sigma := (DirectSum.sigmaFiberLinearEquiv R f (fun i ↦ ↥(grM i))).toLinearMap
abbrev decomp := (decomposeLinearEquiv grM).toLinearMap
abbrev decomp' : M →ₗ[R] (Dec' R grM f) :=
    lmap (fun _ ↦ DirectSum.coeLinearMap.codRestrict R _) ∘ₗ (sigma R grM f) ∘ₗ (decomp R grM)

instance : (DirectSum.Decomposition (induced_decomposition R grM f) ) :=
  DirectSum.Decomposition.ofLinearMap
    (induced_decomposition R grM f)
    (decomp' R grM f)
    (by
    -- 2 reduction steps:
      rw [← (decomposeLinearEquiv grM).symm.eq_comp_toLinearMap_iff _ _]
      apply linearMap_ext
    -- now simplify everything:
      unfold decomp' Dec' induced_decomposition
      intro i
      ext m
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, lmap_comp, LinearEquiv.comp_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
        Function.comp_apply, lof_eq_of, decomposeLinearEquiv_symm_apply, decompose_symm_of,
        LinearEquiv.trans_apply, decomposeLinearEquiv_apply, decompose_coe,
        sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of, lmap_of, coeLinearMap_of, LinearEquiv.coe_ofEq_apply,
        LinearMap.codRestrict_apply, LinearMap.id_comp, decomposeLinearEquiv_symm_comp_lof,
        Submodule.subtype_apply]
        -- last step is found by `simp?`
    ) (by
    -- 3 reduction steps:
      apply linearMap_ext
      intro j
      unfold induced_decomposition -- needed in v4.29r8, but not in v4.28.0
      rw [← LinearMap.cancel_right
        (coeLinearMap.codRestrict_surjective R (fun (i : { i : ι₁ // f i = j}) ↦ ((grM ↑i))))]
      apply linearMap_ext
    -- now simplify everything:
      unfold decomp' Dec' induced_decomposition
      intro ⟨i, hi⟩
      subst hi
      ext m : 1
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, lmap_comp, LinearEquiv.comp_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
        Function.comp_apply, lof_eq_of, coeLinearMap_of, LinearEquiv.coe_ofEq_apply,
        LinearMap.codRestrict_apply, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, decomposeLinearEquiv_apply,
        decompose_coe, sigmaFiberLinearEquiv_of, lmap_of, LinearMap.id_comp]
        -- last step is found by `simp?`
    )

Background: I'd like to define Milnor K-theory as a graded algebra, and to get the grading I would like to start with the (existing) grading on the tensor algebra and use the (non-existent) lemma that a graded ring modulo a homogeneous ideal inherits a canonical grading. So I need to get my head around graded modules and algebras in Lean. The above "push-forward" constructions is just a preliminary exercise. But it could also be applied to obtain a ℤ/2-grading on the tensor algebra from the (existing) ℤ-grading, and then the lemma about quotients by homogeneous ideals would give a new and more canonical construction of the grading on Clifford algebras.

I have been trying to do something similar for my own project, but I have been unable to produce anything useful. I took a look at your code and it seems that some of the statements are abusing def-eq. For example, the ms on each side of DirectSum.lequivCongrLeft_of live in different types. I tried to clean it up, but ran into lots of type-incorrectness problems. Anyway, I just want to say that this is interesting to more than one person, and it seems to be hard to get it right.

I'm glad to hear I'm not the only one finding this difficult. A cleaner version was recently merged into Mathlib:
<https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39607>
